evidence: Meta describes a single place for business activity on Facebook, Messenger, and Instagram, including notifications/messages, content creation and scheduling, and insights.
designTakeaway: Keep business context and related work predictable without copying every feature into one screen.
limitations: Vendor overview only; not a logged-in UI inspection and not evidence that The Social Base APIs offer the same capabilities.

evidence: Buffer describes week/month calendars, channel/tag/post-type filters, drafts, editing posts from the calendar, and separate text boxes per network.
designTakeaway: Use a calendar/queue for planning and keep per-channel text edits close to the shared draft.
limitations: Vendor product page; plan eligibility and actual interface details may vary.

evidence: Hootsuite describes list and calendar views for paid and organic content, collaboration, and approval workflows.
designTakeaway: Keep review and content status close to the planning surface.
limitations: Vendor product page; advanced team workflows are not currently supported in The Social Base.

evidence: Planable describes Feed, Calendar, Grid, and List views, previews and feedback in context, plus labels and brand/client workspaces.
designTakeaway: Show content in its relevant preview and keep brand context clear; start with only the views users need.
limitations: Vendor product page; its permissions and collaboration model exceed the current product scope.

evidence: Later describes a visual calendar/feed planner, media folders, and cross-platform posts tailored per profile.
designTakeaway: Make reusable media easy to find and platform-specific changes easy to make.
limitations: Vendor product page; feature availability depends on product plan and connected platform.

evidence: The free plan is limited by connected accounts and queued posts; paid plans add reusable workspaces, custom variants, calendar and queue scheduling, analytics, approvals, and API/MCP capabilities.
designTakeaway: Expose queue limits, channel-specific variants, and the next available setup step before a user schedules.
limitations: Pricing and capabilities change by billing cadence, number of accounts, and plan.

evidence: The free tier allows one brand, 20 scheduled posts monthly, competitor profiles, and 30 days of analytics; higher tiers add more brands, team/client management, roles, approvals, and reporting.
designTakeaway: Make brand limits and analytics coverage explicit in the workspace and reporting views.
limitations: Prices vary by currency, billing schedule, and brand count.

evidence: Plan features scale from solo scheduling and analytics to bulk scheduling, inbox, team collaboration, client approvals, and white-label reporting.
designTakeaway: Keep team review and client-facing reporting visible as distinct steps in agency workflows.
limitations: Prices and account caps depend on tier and annual billing.

evidence: The plans organize connected channels into brands and progressively add collaboration, workflow approvals, analytics and client portals.
designTakeaway: Use clear brand boundaries and explain how many channels are included in each brand.
limitations: Pricing is regional and varies between monthly and annual billing.

evidence: Plans scale by workspaces for clients/brands and add assignment, approvals, libraries, campaigns, reporting and role controls.
designTakeaway: Let agencies see workspace count and client separation as a first-order setup choice.
limitations: Pricing depends on workspace count and billing cadence; country selection changes displayed prices.

evidence: Scheduling supports specific time, AutoSchedule slots, recurring posts, and recycling; reminder-based manual publication is a separate mode for selected platform actions.
designTakeaway: Represent publishing mode per network variant and keep queue time distinct from confirmed provider publication.
limitations: Behavior and schedule limits depend on plan, platform and account type; help article describes Publer behavior only.

evidence: Calendar sharing allows collaborators to review the planner and reports and take approval actions based on assigned role.
designTakeaway: Keep client review and reporting connected to the brand planner while applying role-based access.
limitations: Plan eligibility and the exact reviewer experience can vary.

evidence: Posts can pass manager review and then optional client review; send-back comments return work for correction, and clients can act through portal or approval links.
designTakeaway: Make approval steps ordered and version-specific; record reviewer identity, comments, and return state.
limitations: Feature access depends on account and plan configuration.

evidence: The All Channels view consolidates posts across channels, including approvals, while account permissions govern who can act.
designTakeaway: Provide a combined action inbox without weakening per-workspace and per-account authorization.
limitations: Team and approval features vary by plan and account permission.
